title: From the Parent's Coincidence to an Explicit Closed Form
content: The docstring frames the open question. The parent (euler-totient-oq-01-oq-02) records only the coincidence λ(pᵏ) = φ(pᵏ) for odd primes, leaving λ's value implicit, and focuses on the non-cyclic 2-power case λ(2ᵏ) = 2ᵏ⁻². This entry supplies the explicit polynomial λ(pᵏ) = pᵏ⁻¹(p − 1) and exposes the full chain that produces it: (ℤ/pᵏℤ)ˣ cyclic ⟹ exponent = order ⟹ λ(pᵏ) = φ(pᵏ) = pᵏ⁻¹(p − 1), plus a named primitive root and five concrete values.
mathContext: $\lambda(p^k) = p^{k-1}(p-1)$ for odd prime $p$, $k\ge 1$ — the explicit form behind the parent's implicit $\lambda(p^k)=\varphi(p^k)$.
prerequisites: exponent and order of a group

title: The Cyclic Mechanism: Exponent = Order
content: isCyclic_units_odd_prime_pow is Gauss's primitive-root theorem in Mathlib form: for an odd prime p, the unit group (ℤ/pᵏℤ)ˣ is cyclic (ZMod.isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow). exponent_units_odd_prime_pow then applies IsCyclic.iff_exponent_eq_card — in a finite cyclic group the exponent equals the cardinality. Since the Carmichael function λ is by definition the exponent of (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ and φ is its cardinality, this single equality is the entire reason λ(pᵏ) = φ(pᵏ). It is the sharp opposite of the parent's 2-power case, where the non-cyclic ℤ/2 × ℤ/2ᵏ⁻² forces λ = φ/2.

title: λ(pᵏ) = φ(pᵏ): The Parent's Coincidence Restated
content: carmichael_eq_totient restates the parent's carmichael_pow_of_prime_ne_two: for an odd prime p, λ(pᵏ) = φ(pᵏ). This is the direct consequence of exponent = order (λ is the exponent, φ the order). Keeping it as a named lemma here makes the entry self-contained and marks the precise point where the cyclic regime diverges from the 2-power case λ(2ᵏ) = φ(2ᵏ)/2.
mathContext: $\lambda(p^k) = \varphi(p^k)$ for odd prime $p$ — exponent equals order.

title: The Closed Form λ(pᵏ) = pᵏ⁻¹(p − 1)
content: carmichael_odd_prime_pow is the open question's target: rewrite λ(pᵏ) = φ(pᵏ) (carmichael_pow_of_prime_ne_two, the cyclic coincidence) with φ(pᵏ) = pᵏ⁻¹(p − 1) (Nat.totient_prime_pow) to turn the implicit value φ(pᵏ) into an explicit polynomial in p and k. carmichael_odd_prime is the k = 1 corollary λ(p) = p − 1, obtained by specialising at k = 1 and simplifying — the multiplicative group of the finite field 𝔽_p, cyclic of order p − 1.
relatedConcepts: multiplicative group of a finite field

title: A Primitive Root of Order Exactly φ(pᵏ)
content: exists_primitiveRoot_odd_prime_pow makes cyclicity constructive: it names an actual unit g of order exactly pᵏ⁻¹(p − 1) — a primitive root modulo pᵏ, whose powers exhaust every unit. The generator comes from IsCyclic.exists_ofOrder_eq_natCard, and its order is identified with the closed form by transporting through Nat.card = Fintype.card = #(ℤ/pᵏℤ)ˣ = φ(pᵏ) = pᵏ⁻¹(p − 1) (ZMod.card_units_eq_totient, Nat.totient_prime_pow). This partially answers the parent's follow-up on which moduli admit primitive roots.
prerequisites: existence of a generator in a cyclic group
card of the unit group = totient

title: Concrete Values Across Two Odd Primes
content: The five evaluations instantiate the closed form: λ(9) = 3¹·2 = 6, λ(27) = 3²·2 = 18, λ(25) = 5¹·4 = 20, λ(7) = 7 − 1 = 6, λ(49) = 7¹·6 = 42. In each case λ(pᵏ) = φ(pᵏ) (full totient), the visible numerical signature of the cyclic regime — contrast λ(8) = 2 = φ(8)/2 in the parent. All follow from carmichael_odd_prime_pow (or carmichael_odd_prime for λ(7)) by reducing the power with norm_num (no native_decide), so they stay kernel-checked and axiom-free.
